title: Self-Ext to dual self-Tor cap comparison on regular affine charts
statement: For any closed immersion i:Z -> Y [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-scheme], natural number n and derived category of module sheaves on Y [def-pc-derived-category], let B=i_*O_Z, G=H^n(RHom_Y(B[0],B[0])) [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and Q=i*H^{-n}(B[0] tensor^L B[0]), using the fixed derived tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure, def-pc-module-pullback]. There exists a global morphism kappa: i*G -> dual(Q) [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. For every open V of Z and affine U of Y whose immersion ideal is spanned by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence], its restriction to V and then to the over site of V intersect i^{-1}(U) is an isomorphism [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. No conormal comparison or overlap compatibility is asserted.

proof.text: For B=i_*O_Z let G=H^n RHom_Y(B[0],B[0]) and Q=i*H^{-n}(B[0] tensor^L B[0]). Construct the canonical cap pairing of the Ext and Tor sheaves. A local Ext class is a derived morphism B -> B[n]; tensor it with B and take degree-minus-n homology to get Tor_n(B,B) -> Tor_0(B,B)=B. In a free resolution on an affine chart this is evaluation of a Hom(P,B) cocycle on a cycle of P tensor B. Boundaries evaluate to zero, and resolution comparison preserves this evaluation. Internal derived Hom and its open restriction identify these local pairings with the Ext sheaf G. This defines a restriction-compatible sheaf pairing, including on singular charts.

The quotient ideal acts by zero on B and on Tor. Consequently the pairing factors through tensor-pullback to Z and takes values in O_Z. By internal tensor--Hom currying it defines a global morphism kappa: i*G -> dual(Q). The construction uses the actual fixed derived tensor and RHom, not a newly chosen derived structure. It does not refer to a conormal sheaf or an exterior comparison.

On a regular affine chart choose the Koszul projective resolution and sheafify its augmentation. The bounded finite free Hom complex computes RHom. Hom into B and tensor with B both have zero differential. The cap pairing is the evaluation pairing Hom_A(K_n,B) times (K_n tensor_A B) -> B. A finite increasing-wedge basis makes the resulting map into the B-dual an isomorphism. Localization preserves the pairing, and restriction therefore gives an isomorphism on each over site in the statement.

At n=0 evaluation is multiplication on B. For n greater than the number of generators the two modules vanish. The zero quotient ring, empty inverse-image charts and generator length zero satisfy the same calculation. Restriction to an arbitrary V preserves the chart isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem selfExt_tor_dual_chart
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (n : ℕ) :
    let B := (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf)
    let S := DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0
    let H := derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) Y.toRingedSpace.sheaf
    let G := (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) (n : ℤ)).obj
        (H.obj (op (S.obj B), S.obj B))
    let Q := (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) (-(n : ℤ))).obj
          (S.obj B ⊗ S.obj B))
    ∃ κ : (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj G ⟶ Scheme.Modules.dual Q,
      ∀ (V : Z.Opens) (U : Y.affineOpens)
        (_hU : ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : Fin m → Γ(Y, U.1)),
          Ideal.span (Set.range f) = i.ker.ideal U ∧
            RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular f),
        IsIso (((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).map κ).over
          (V.ι ⁻¹ᵁ (i ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)))
